subject: Request: temporary burst window & priority policy for Zenith Labs product launch
messages:
From: Alex Geller <alex.geller@zenithlabs.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@zenithlabs.ai>
Date: 2027-11-20T09:03:00Z
Subject: Request: temporary burst window & priority policy for Zenith Labs product launch

Hi Sofia,

We have a hard launch on 2027-11-25 for our consumer-facing model, and the first 36 hours are expected to see large bursts from onboarding cohorts. Our infra team estimates peak request rate ~9k reqs/minute with average prompt size ~450 tokens.

We are asking Redwood for a temporary burst policy change: allow a prioritized burst window for 48 hours (2027-11-25 00:00 UTC -> 2027-11-27 00:00 UTC) with a short-term quota uplift and a fairness priority (requests from official tenant API keys should be favored vs public demo traffic). We'll accept reasonable rate-based fees for the uplift.

Attached: zenith_launch_summary.pdf (high level traffic and go-live plan). Can you confirm feasibility and any doc/approval you need to proceed?

Thanks,
Alex
VP, Product
Zenith Labs

---
Attachment: zenith_launch_summary.pdf (pdf, 2 pages)

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Geller <alex.geller@zenithlabs.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-20T11:15:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: temporary burst window & priority policy for Zenith Labs product launch

Hi Alex — thanks for the heads up and the summary. We can support temporary uplift windows carefully, but we'll need a short mutual action plan and a few technical details to scope the change safely:

- Exact expected sustained RPS and peak P95 latency target you need to hit during the window.
- Which API keys/tenant IDs should receive the prioritized treatment?
- Any tolerance for degraded quality vs fallback models if capacity is saturated?

Operationally, options are:
- Temporary quota bump + priority queueing for specified tenant keys (fastest path, but we impose a hard cap to protect fairness).
- Short TTL KV cache tweaks and batched responses to reduce token cost during the window.
- Fallback policy: automatic degrade to a lower-cost/shorter-context model if the primary model hits sustained token limits.

I'm looping in Rishi (serving/runtime) and Priyom (partner/sales ops) to advise on the config and pricing. I've included a mutual action plan template (redwood_map_template.xlsx). If you can populate the expected RPS and tenant ids today, we can aim to produce a conditional approval with terms by EOD.

Sofia Ivanova
Senior Director, Commercial
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: redwood_map_template.xlsx (xlsx, 1 sheet)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-20T15:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: temporary burst window & priority policy for Zenith Labs product launch

Sofia — quick technical readout based on Alex's numbers:

Summary recommendation:
- Approve a 48-hour prioritized burst window (2027-11-25 00:00 -> 2027-11-27 00:00 UTC) with an explicit hard cap of 14M tokens/hour for the prioritized tenant to limit downstream impact.
- Implement request tagging by tenant API key and a priority queue that favors those tags for scheduling onto dedicated warm GPU pools.
- Apply a transient fairness throttle: if cluster-wide utilization > 92% for > 5min, dynamically reduce per-tenant priority factor to preserve baseline SLOs for other customers.
- Fallback: auto-route to a compatible 8-bit quantized variant of the model with a shorter context (reduces latency and token cost) if average queue latency exceeds 250ms.

Operational notes:
- We need the tenant API keys and an anonymized sample of request distribution by minute to simulate prefix caching benefit (helps sizing).
- Security/compliance: no changes to data retention or logging. Any changes will run in the hosted environment unless customer requests Private deployment.

I'll stand up a short runbook with exact config knobs and rollback criteria. From a capacity standpoint this is feasible with a short notice change; pricing should include an uplift fee and an overage rate for any tokens beyond the hard cap.

Rishi Malhotra
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

---

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Geller <alex.geller@zenithlabs.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@zenithlabs.ai>
Date: 2027-11-21T08:40:00Z
Subject: RE: Request: temporary burst window & priority policy for Zenith Labs product launch

Alex — following internal review we've provisionally approved the temporary burst window with the following conditional terms: 

1) Window: 2027-11-25 00:00 UTC -> 2027-11-27 00:00 UTC (48 hours).
2) Prioritized quota: tenant keys provided by Zenith Labs will receive prioritized scheduling up to a hard cap of 14M tokens/hour.
3) Fairness fallback: if Redwood cluster utilization > 92% for longer than 5 minutes, priority factors will be automatically scaled down to preserve platform-wide SLOs.
4) Fallback model: auto-route affected traffic to a compatible quantized variant if queue latency > 250ms.
5) Pricing: one-time uplift fee (to be agreed) + overage billing at the agreed per-token rate beyond the hard cap.
6) No changes to data retention or logging; all requests processed under existing terms.

Next steps — please:
- Reply with the tenant API keys to prioritize and a minute-level request sample CSV by EOD 2027-11-21 so Rishi's team can run sizing simulations.
- Sign the short-term amendment (I've attached the sla-priority-term-sheet.pdf) and route via DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/sign/ZXNhbXBsZS1kb2N1c2lnbg

If you need a narrower window or a different cap, we can discuss but that may change pricing or rollback criteria. Once we have the API keys and the signed amendment we'll finalize the configuration and provide the runbook and monitoring dashboard link.

Thanks — looking forward to supporting the launch.

Sofia Ivanova
Senior Director, Commercial
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: sla-priority-term-sheet.pdf (pdf, 3 pages)
